nodes.label: Tauri v2 externalBin sidecar
nodes.summary: `bundle.externalBin` in tauri.conf.json is a list of absolute or tauri.conf-relative paths, resolved against `src-tauri/`. A file with the same name plus a `-$TARGET_TRIPLE` suffix must exist (`my-sidecar-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` on Linux, `.exe` appended on Windows; triple from `rustc --print host-tuple`). `copy_binaries()` strips the `-{target}` suffix when copying into the bundle. Spawning is `app.shell().sidecar("my-sidecar")?.spawn()` via `tauri_plugin_shell::ShellExt`, passing the filename only, and requires `shell:allow-execute` or `shell:allow-spawn` plus a scope entry `{"name": "binaries/my-sidecar", "sidecar": true}` in `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`, with `.plugin(tauri_plugin_shell::init())` registered in Rust. Snipset registers only `process`, `globalShortcut`, `updater` and has no `binaries/` directory, so a sidecar would be net-new.

nodes.label: AppImage bundler mutates the sidecar ELF, deb does not
nodes.norm_label: appimage bundler mutates the sidecar elf, deb does not
nodes.summary: The same sidecar arrives in two packages as two different binaries. In tauri issue #5445 the md5sum is e7749750 in `binaries/`, 546f08b0 in `target/release/sidecar` and identically 546f08b0 inside the deb, but 758df01d inside the AppImage, where the copy crashed. The mechanism is in tauri issue #11898 (open, `status: upstream`, Linux): linuxdeploy strips the binary and rewrites its RPATH to `$ORIGIN/../lib`, which broke a Nuitka standalone sidecar; the reporter's workaround is `NO_STRIP=1`. Whether strip plus patchelf breaks a PyInstaller onefile is UNVERIFIED — PyInstaller onefile is not RPATH-dependent, so it is likely fine, but it must be smoke-tested against the real AppImage.

nodes.label: GUI apps on Linux and macOS do not inherit $PATH from shell dotfiles
nodes.norm_label: gui apps on linux and macos do not inherit $path from shell dotfiles
nodes.summary: Tauri states that GUI apps on macOS and Linux do not inherit the $PATH from shell dotfiles and recommends the `fix-path-env-rs` crate. This kills any "just exec `yt-dlp` by name" design and any reliance on a bare runtime name, and it is called the single most common sidecar bug. The same gap reappears for the JavaScript engine yt-dlp-ejs needs, since only deno is enabled by default and must be findable on PATH or named explicitly with `--js-runtimes`.

nodes.label: yt-dlp PyInstaller GPLv3+ licensing trap for vendoring
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp pyinstaller gplv3+ licensing trap for vendoring
nodes.summary: Upstream states the PyInstaller-bundled executables include GPLv3+ licensed code and the combined work is therefore GPLv3+. `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` names the Linux-specific cause: GNU Readline, GPL-3.0-or-later, "Only included in Linux builds". Snipset's `tauri.conf.json:78` declares `license: "Proprietary"` with an all-rights-reserved LICENSE, so shipping `yt-dlp_linux` or `yt-dlp_musllinux` as a sidecar would make Snipset GPLv3+. The zipimport `yt-dlp` and `yt-dlp.tar.gz` carry only ISC (`meriyah`) and MIT (`astring`) on top of yt-dlp's own Unlicense, and are safe for a proprietary bundle. Documented upstream, not legal advice.

nodes.label: yt-dlp standalone binary vendoring on Linux
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp standalone binary vendoring on linux
nodes.summary: yt-dlp can be shipped inside the app rather than required from the user. Release assets are `yt-dlp` (platform-independent zipimport, needs Python 3.10+, upstream-recommended for Linux/BSD), `yt-dlp_linux` / `_aarch64` (PyInstaller, glibc 2.17+) and `yt-dlp_musllinux*`; both the PyInstaller and official zipimport builds bundle `yt-dlp-ejs`. A copy frozen at app-build time is already 6-12 months behind nightly on release day given a 6-12 month app cadence, and pinned issue #3766 lists multiple YouTube breakages currently fixed only in nightly or master, so the vendored copy has to be updatable independently of the app. The pattern recommended is a known-good sidecar in the bundle for offline first run plus a user-triggered updater that fetches the zipimport asset and SHA2-256SUMS into `$XDG_DATA_HOME/Snipset/yt-dlp/`, with the bundled copy as fallback.

nodes.label: yt-dlp-ejs JavaScript runtime requirement
nodes.summary: Full YouTube support needs `yt-dlp-ejs`, which the official builds already bundle, plus a JavaScript engine: deno >= 2.3.0 (enabled by default), node >= 22 via `--js-runtimes node`, or QuickJS; bun support is deprecated. Because GUI apps do not inherit $PATH the engine will not be found, so the app must either ship a second sidecar for deno (roughly 40 MB) or resolve a system runtime and pass `--js-runtimes "node:/usr/bin/node"`, degrading to a clear error when absent. This is a second hidden runtime dependency on top of yt-dlp itself, and the only fully self-contained answer is shipping both as sidecars.

nodes.label: Flatpak reserved paths make a host yt-dlp unreachable
nodes.norm_label: flatpak reserved paths make a host yt-dlp unreachable
nodes.summary: A Flatpak sandbox cannot spawn an arbitrary host binary. The sandbox permissions doc gives "No access to processes outside the sandbox", no host files beyond the runtime, the app, `~/.var/app/$FLATPAK_ID` and `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app/$FLATPAK_ID`, and a reserved-paths list — `/app, /bin, /dev, /etc, /lib, /lib32, /lib64, /proc, /run/flatpak, /run/host, /sbin, /usr` — where "asking access to them with `--filesystem` will have no effect". So `--filesystem=host` cannot expose `/usr/bin/yt-dlp`. The only routes are bundling yt-dlp inside the Flatpak or an extension, and extensions mount under `/app/extension_directory/...` with no property that extends PATH, so the binary must be invoked by absolute path. Flatpak is out of scope today: `tauri.conf.json:73` targets msi, nsis, deb, appimage, and Tauri v2's `PackageType` enum has no Flatpak target at all.

nodes.label: yt-dlp -U cannot self-update inside a read-only bundle
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp -u cannot self-update inside a read-only bundle
nodes.summary: `yt_dlp/update.py` checks `os.access(self.filename, os.W_OK)` and `os.access(directory, os.W_OK)` before updating and otherwise reports 'Insufficient permissions to write to ...'. Both fail for a bundled sidecar: an AppImage sidecar sits on the read-only squashfs mount, and a deb install puts it under `/usr/lib/Snipset/`, which a non-root user cannot write. `_NON_UPDATEABLE_REASONS` also marks a package-manager install as non-updateable, and onedir builds as "Auto-update is not supported for unpackaged executables". So a shipped yt-dlp cannot be kept current by its own updater; the app has to own that updater.

nodes.label: yt-dlp release signatures cover only the checksum manifest and the updater ignores them
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp release signatures cover only the checksum manifest and the updater ignores them
nodes.summary: yt-dlp does publish `SHA2-256SUMS` / `SHA2-512SUMS` with `.sig` GPG signature files and a `public.key`, verifiable offline against the manifest — but there is no minisign, no Sigstore or GitHub artifact attestation, and no per-binary detached signature. The built-in updater downloads SHA2-256SUMS from the same release and never touches the `.sig`, so a checksum from the same host as the payload gives no third-party trust anchor. When the hash is missing it only warns ('The hash could not be found in the checksum file, skipping verification') and still writes the file, blocking only the auto-restart (yt-dlp issue #17550). Because `public.key` is a plain file in the same repository as the release, the app must hardcode the key fingerprint in Rust for verification to mean anything.

nodes.label: Distro yt-dlp staleness and open CVEs rule out depending on a system package
nodes.norm_label: distro yt-dlp staleness and open cves rule out depending on a system package
nodes.summary: As of 2026-09-26 Arch `extra` carries 2026.08.19-1 (~5 weeks old, with `python` and `yt-dlp-ejs` hard deps), Debian stable 2025.04.30-1 (~17 months), Ubuntu noble 2024.04.09-1 (~29 months) and Debian oldstable 2023.03.04-1 (~3.5 years). Debian stable predates every fix for the five open tracker issues (CVE-2026-50019, -50023, -50574, -55404, -26331, fixed 2026.02 to 2026.07). A distro package also cannot be updated by the app — `_NON_UPDATEABLE_REASONS` maps variant `unknown` to "You installed yt-dlp from a manual build or with a package manager" and the FAQ says "there is nothing we can do if your distribution serves an outdated/broken version". pipx and AUR helpers are worse: pipx needs both pipx and Python and puts the binary on a $PATH a GUI app cannot see, and yt-dlp is already in `extra`, so an AUR helper is unnecessary and not guaranteed present.
